title: The Broken Compass
premise: Lena Halloran, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted after a rescue gone wrong in Kyrgyzstan, scrapes by leading illegal treks along the Himalayan fringe with a found-family crew of misfits. When her old rival Dev Kapoor arrives with a contract to follow the Tsangpo's headwaters to a forbidden glacial source—ground Lena swore off after her brother vanished there years ago—she refuses, until the client reveals he has evidence that could clear her name and news that her brother may still be alive. As monsoon clouds gather, the crew races upstream through checkpoints, collapsing ice bridges, and the lies they've told each other for a decade. In the end, Lena reaches the source and finds not her brother but his final letters and a surviving member of his lost expedition; she chooses truth over absolution, turning down the pardon to bring the man home instead.
about_author: B. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent eight seasons in the Karakoram before trading base camps for a writing desk in Vancouver. Their fiction draws on real route notes, rescued journals, and the quiet debts climbers owe each other.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She leads an off-book trek through Nepali backcountry, dodging rangers and lying smoothly to clients about her past. A checkpoint scare reminds her how thin her invisibility is. Emotional beat: competence as armor, loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back in Pokhara, we meet the crew: gruff cook Tomas, navigator Priya hiding her own record, teenage runner Kip who idolizes Lena. A shared meal sketches their found family. Emotional beat: warmth earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Man from Kathmandu
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev Kapoor, once Lena's closest climbing partner, now a polished outfitter, arrives with a contract and old guilt. He watches her crew from across the market, rehearsing what he'll say. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in ambition.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Dev makes his offer: guide him upriver to the Tsangpo's forbidden source. Lena throws him out, naming the one valley she'll never enter—the one that took her brother Eli. Emotional beat: rage masking grief.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Dev left behind a dossier: satellite photos, an official report on Eli's lost expedition, and a line suggesting a survivor was extracted alive. She hides it, torn between loyalty and hope. Emotional beat: temptation.

chapters.title: The Price of a Pardon
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Sleepless, Lena reads the dossier alone. The evidence could end her blacklist—but only if the source survey is completed. She hates that hope feels like betrayal. Emotional beat: grief reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Negotiation at the teahouse: Dev offers full pay, gear, and the exoneration file upon completion. Lena sets her own term—if there's any trace of Eli, the job stops. He agrees too easily. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Packing for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kip's POV. Preparations: bribes, permits forged, Kip stowing away-adjacent as the youngest hire. He notices Lena packing Eli's old compass, its needle cracked. Emotional beat: hero worship meeting human fragility.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The expedition enters the river gorge. Beauty and menace in equal measure; Dev's modern equipment clashes with Lena's instinct-led style. First friction over route choice. Emotional beat: two philosophies of survival colliding.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Suspension Bridge
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Soldiers question the convoy; Tomas bluffs with forged timber permits while Priya reroutes mules through a landslide scar. They pass, barely. Emotional beat: the crew discovering how much they trust each other.

chapters.title: Old Routes, New Rules
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confesses part of his motive: his company is failing, and this survey is his last card. Lena gives him cold mercy. Emotional beat: rivalry softening into something more dangerous—understanding.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew shelters in a hidden village whose elders remember Eli's expedition—and remember it badly. An old woman gives Lena a weathered carabiner stamped with Eli's initials. Emotional beat: the past arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Monsoon Watch
chapters.summary: Kip's POV. Weather radio crackles: the monsoon is early. Dev wants to push on; Tomas argues to turn back. Lena casts the deciding vote—onward. Emotional beat: leadership as a lonely arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ice Bridge
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Crossing a crevassed glacier, a bridge collapses under a porter; Lena's rope work saves him, echoing the rescue that ruined her. This time no one dies—and it changes nothing about how she feels. Emotional beat: skill without redemption.

chapters.title: What Dev Didn't Burn
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Privately, Dev admits to himself he knew about the survivor extraction years ago and said nothing. Flashback to the aftermath of Eli's disappearance and the choice that made his career. Emotional beat: guilt calcifying into cowardice.

chapters.title: Night Talk
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Lena share watch; Priya reveals why she was blacklisted—she falsified a client's summit record to save his life. Two liars recognizing each other. Emotional beat: intimacy built from shared shame.

chapters.title: The Gorge Narrows
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Terrain turns vertical; porters quit. The crew ropes together through a slot canyon as rain begins in earnest. Kip slips; Lena catches him by the pack strap. Emotional beat: fear sharpening love.

chapters.title: Forbidden Ground
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They cross the boundary ridge into the closed valley. Every step is trespass now. Tomas writes a letter home he may never send. Emotional beat: crossing from risk into transgression.

chapters.title: Eli's Cache
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following the old woman's directions, they find a supply cache Eli hid twelve years ago—intact, deliberate, meant to be found. Inside: a journal page pointing higher, toward 'the eye of the river.' Emotional beat: hope arriving like vertigo.

chapters.title: The Journal Pages
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev reads over Lena's shoulder and realizes Eli had discovered something the client wants buried—a mineral survey, or worse. Dev says nothing. Emotional beat: complicity deepening.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A pre-monsoon storm pins them for three days in a snow cave. Rations halved. Kip's fever spikes; Priya trades her own food to him. Emotional beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: Confession at Altitude
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Delirious-adjacent honesty around the stove: Lena tells Dev she doesn't want the pardon anymore—she wants the truth about Eli. Dev almost tells her what he knows. Doesn't. Emotional beat: the lie becoming load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Client Calls
chapters.summary: Kip's POV. Satellite phone call: the client orders them to abandon the search for remains and proceed straight to the source coordinates. Dev agrees without consulting Lena. Kip overhears everything. Emotional beat: the first crack in the alliance.

chapters.title: Mutiny at High Camp
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Kip tells the crew. Confrontation in the tents: Tomas threatens to turn back, Priya sides with Lena, Dev invokes the contract. Lena splits the difference—source first, then answers. Emotional beat: family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Eye of the River
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They reach the glacial cirque: the source, a blue-black lake under a hanging serac, more violent and beautiful than any map suggested. Survey instruments come out. Lena looks past them, searching for her brother. Emotional beat: arrival that feels like loss.

chapters.title: The Serac Fails
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The ice cliff calves; the lake surges. Dev shoves Priya clear and is swept toward the outflow channel, clinging to a rock fin. Emotional beat: cowardice finally spending itself in one honest act.

chapters.title: Rope of Three
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena, Tomas, and Kip run a tension traverse into the flood channel to pull Dev out. It works—barely. Dev, coughing water, starts talking before anyone asks. Emotional beat: rescue as confession.

chapters.title: Everything Dev Knows
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Full confession: the survivor was extracted secretly by the client's company; Eli died covering the retreat; the client has been erasing the valley ever since. The pardon was bait. Emotional beat: ruin and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The client calls again demanding the data. Lena burns the survey cards and keeps only Eli's journal. Whatever comes next, it won't be bought. Emotional beat: duty inverted—loyalty to the dead over freedom for herself.

chapters.title: Descent Before the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The sky opens. The crew descends the gorge in full monsoon, leeches, landslides, and all, moving like the unit they've become. Priya navigates by memory and nerve. Emotional beat: found family functioning as one body.

chapters.title: The Landslide
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A slope lets go; the trail vanishes behind them and takes most of the gear. Tomas injures his ankle shielding Kip. They are slower now, and hunted. Emotional beat: sacrifice without complaint.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In a herder's hut above the tree line they find him: Anselm Reyes, frostbitten ghost of Eli's expedition, who has hidden in the valley for twelve years rather than testify. He recognizes Eli's compass. Emotional beat: grief and closure colliding mid-breath.

chapters.title: Anselm's Story
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV (interleaved with Lena's). Around the fire, Anselm recounts the disaster and Eli's last hours—how Eli stayed with a fallen teammate so no one would die alone. He kept silent out of fear and shame. Emotional beat: the truth as both wound and gift.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev proposes going public—not for the pardon, but to force the company to account. He'll lose everything. Lena believes him this time because he's choosing the loss. Emotional beat: redemption accepted, not granted.

chapters.title: Running the Border
chapters.summary: Kip's POV. The final flight downstream: soldiers at the last bridge, Anselm too weak to run. Kip creates a diversion with the sat phone and firecrackers, nearly getting caught. Emotional beat: the kid earning his place in the story.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Safe in Kathmandu, they deliver Anselm and the journal to journalists and the mountaineering federation. The blacklist inquiry reopens; the client's company unravels publicly. Emotional beat: justice arriving quietly, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The pardon comes through—full reinstatement, offers from three outfitters. Lena reads the letter twice and files it away unanswered. Some doors you don't walk back through. Emotional beat: freedom feeling strangely like an ending.

chapters.title: The Compass Mended
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A jeweler in Thamel repairs Eli's cracked compass. Lena donates the journal to the expedition museum but keeps the carabiner. She visits Anselm, who is learning to walk again. Emotional beat: carrying the dead forward instead of being carried by them.

chapters.title: New Routes
chapters.summary: Kip's POV. One year later: the crew launches a small ethical guiding outfit—no forbidden valleys, no bought names. Kip leads his first client trek, using Lena's rope calls. Emotional beat: legacy passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Source
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena returns alone—not to the forbidden lake, but to a high meadow where she scatters Eli's journal copy pages to the wind and finally weeps. Downstream, the river runs on. Emotional beat: grief integrated; the journey complete.
